title: What is Home Science
summary: Home Science is the science of managing a home. It covers ourselves, our home, family members and resources, and aims at the greatest satisfaction for the family through efficient and scientific use of resources. It is the art of managing resources efficiently and the science of achieving a healthy, happy home and a successful career. Knowing the nutrients the body needs is the science; choosing dishes that have them and serving them attractively is the art.

Home Science draws content from physics, chemistry, biology, physiology and hygiene, and equally from economics, sociology, anthropology, psychology, community development, communication, media and technology, so it is an interdisciplinary field of science and arts. Its areas are communication among family members, the family, food, the house, clothes, resources, the environment and the skills for a career.

Earlier, work was divided between men and women. Today more women work outside the home, so managing a home needs the efforts of all members and gender-based roles no longer hold. Home Science is for both boys and girls: both share household tasks, manage resources and solve problems together, and both can find varied careers in it. It also helps to set up home-based enterprises such as a boutique, catering unit, creche or day care centre.

Five major areas: Food and Nutrition (food science, clinical and community nutrition, institutional food service); Resource Management (housing and equipment, interior decoration, consumer education); Fabric and Apparel Science (clothing construction, textile science, garment designing, care of clothes); Human Development (child welfare, adolescence, marriage and family guidance, care of the elderly and special children); Communication and Extension (media, programme planning and evaluation, training, management of community service organisations). These courses are offered at graduate and postgraduate level and through distance education; NIOS offers vocational courses.

Wage employment means working for another person and receiving a wage or salary; self-employment means owning, running and financing your own enterprise. A tailor with his own shop is self-employed; the same tailor in a garment factory is in wage employment. Examples: catering (staff in canteen, cook, service staff / owner of a canteen, food service from home); food preservation and bakery (production unit staff / own production unit, home-based production); interior decoration (interior designer, furniture designer, showroom staff / own shop, home-based craft centre); housekeeping and laundry (hotel and guest-house staff, facilities manager / running a guest house, paying-guest service); dress designing (production unit or export house staff, boutique staff / owner of a boutique, hobby classes); teaching (creche, play school, day care, school or college teacher / owner of a creche, tuitions at home); communication and extension (development organisation staff, counsellor, researcher / consultancy, market research, media production); resource management and consumer education (retail staff, event management firm / event manager, small savings agent).
To succeed you need thorough knowledge, practice and experience; the school course gives only basic knowledge, so specific advanced courses are needed for a job.

vsa: Name any four wage-employment opportunities related to foods and nutrition.
Staff in a canteen or restaurant; cook; service staff; staff in a food production unit (preservation, bakery or confectionery); in-charge of a community centre or service.
Mention any four self-employment opportunities available in the field of foods and nutrition.
Owner of a canteen, restaurant or tea/coffee shop; food service from home; conducting hobby classes; home-based production of preserved foods or bakery items; owner of a production unit.
Name two self-employment opportunities for the youth in interior decoration.
Working as an interior designer, furniture designer, showroom or shop owner, show-case and window display designer, running a home-based craft centre or conducting hobby courses (any two).
Give any four reasons why Home Science is relevant to both boys and girls.

Both share household responsibilities; both need to manage resources; problems are solved together by family members; it offers varied vocational and professional avenues to both; joint knowledge and skills raise the standard of living.
Name any four home-based self-employment opportunities for Home Science students.
Boutique or tailoring from home; catering or tiffin service; creche or day care; tuitions or hobby classes; paying-guest service; home-based craft centre; production of pickles, jams or bakery items.
List the five areas of specialisation in Home Science.
Food and Nutrition; Resource Management; Fabric and Apparel Science; Human Development; Communication and Extension.
sa: Explain how Home Science is both an art and a science with two examples.

Home Science is the art of managing resources efficiently and the science of achieving a healthy, happy home. Example 1: learning the nutrients the body needs and their functions is the science; selecting dishes that give them and serving them attractively so that the family eats the right food is the art. Example 2: knowing how germs are removed by soap is science; keeping the house clean and tidy in an aesthetic way is art. It also draws on physics, chemistry, biology, economics, sociology and psychology.
Distinguish between wage employment and self-employment with two examples each.

Wage employment means working for another person and receiving a wage or salary, e.g. staff in a hotel, a boutique or a production unit. Self-employment means that you own, run and finance the enterprise, e.g. owner of a boutique, a creche or a catering unit. A tailor who sets up his own shop is self-employed; if he works in a garment factory for a salary he is in wage employment.
Why do people say that gender-based roles no longer hold in managing a home? Give three reasons.

Today more women work outside the home, so the responsibilities of home and family have to be shared. Both men and women need to manage resources like time, energy and money. Problems are best solved together by all members. Home Science also opens equal careers for boys and girls.
la: Name the five areas of specialisation of Home Science and give two examples of further specialisation in each.

(1) Food and Nutrition – food science, clinical nutrition, community nutrition, institutional food service. (2) Resource Management – housing and equipment, interior decoration, consumer education. (3) Fabric and Apparel Science – clothing construction, textile science, garment designing, care and maintenance of clothes. (4) Human Development – child welfare, adolescence and family guidance, care of the elderly and special children. (5) Communication and Extension – media for communication, programme planning and evaluation, training and capacity building, management of community service organisations. These are studied at graduate and post-graduate level.
List five opportunities each for wage employment and self-employment in the field of Home Science (any areas).

Wage employment: staff in a canteen or restaurant; staff at a hotel or guest house; staff in an export house or boutique; creche or school teacher; staff in a retail outlet or event management firm; researcher in a development organisation. Self-employment: owner of a canteen or restaurant; owner of a boutique; interior or furniture designer with own shop; owner of a creche or day care; conducting hobby classes or tuitions at home; home-based production centre; event manager; small savings agent.
